# cube — template guide

A Cube semantic layer: the data model in YAML under cube/, a local dev server, and a pre-pull-request check that compiles the model in the pinned Cube image and snapshots the SQL of golden queries. It deploys either to Cube Cloud with the cube CLI or, for self-hosted Cube Core, to Kubernetes with a production Helm chart adapted from gadsme's (API instances, a refresh worker, a Cube Store cluster, Prometheus metrics) and an image per data model, with optional GitHub Actions that check every pull request and promote main from staging to production, and deploy hooks for the first deploy. On base: the house editor, git, mise, Paseo, agent-instruction, skill and MCP configuration.

Extends: `../base` (its questions and patches are part of this template)

This directory is a [weft](https://github.com/SoheilSalmani/weft) template.
For the full machine-readable contract run `weft describe --json` here.

## Questions

| id | kind | required | default | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_name` | string | **yes** | — | Human-facing name; becomes the README title and, slugified, the Compose project, the Helm release and namespace, and the local image name. (e.g. `Demo Service`) |
| `use_github` | bool | no | True | Installs the skills for issues, pull requests, README and repository metadata, which drive gh, and GitHub's remote MCP server (a personal access token each person exports as GITHUB_PAT_TOKEN, nothing stored in the repo) for Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi. |
| `use_linear` | bool | no | True | Installs the Linear skills and the Linear remote MCP server (OAuth per user, nothing stored in the repo) for Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi. |
| `use_jira` | bool | no | False | Installs the Jira skills and the Atlassian remote MCP server (OAuth per user, nothing stored in the repo) for Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi. |
| `use_anki` | bool | no | False | Installs anki-flashcards and remembering-what-you-built, and the anki MCP server they call (run by npx against AnkiConnect on localhost, nothing stored in the repo) for Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi. |
| `use_obsidian` | bool | no | False | Installs idea-garden and the MCP server of Obsidian's Local REST API with MCP plugin (its HTTP server turned on and its API key exported as OBSIDIAN_MCP_API_KEY by each person, nothing stored in the repo) for Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi. |
| `use_meetings` | bool | no | False | Installs preparing-client-meetings, which prepares what to say at dailies and weeklies from pull requests and tickets, in a weekly note in the Obsidian vault. The vault is found per machine, so nothing about it is stored in the repo. |
| `use_weft` | bool | no | False | Installs weft-conventions and the skills for creating, extracting and splitting Weft templates. |
| `stack_skills` | choice:  | no |  | Installs the Agent Skills written for one stack: the five dbt skills, Lightdash's three for a dbt project on Lightdash, or writing-slides for a slide deck. Each stack template offers only its own: dbt selects its skills and offers Lightdash's, and slides always installs writing-slides. |
| `commit_skills` | bool | no | True | When false, .agents/ and the .claude/skills/ links are gitignored; weft still renders and updates them, and every new git worktree, Paseo's included, gets a copy from the main checkout. Any false commit_* answer also gitignores paseo.json and .weft/, whose base.json holds a copy of every rendered file. |
| `commit_mcp` | bool | no | True | When false, .mcp.json, .codex/ and .omp/ are gitignored and copied into every new git worktree instead. Asked whatever servers the other answers turn on, since a stack can add its own server to them. Any false commit_* answer also gitignores paseo.json and .weft/. |
| `commit_mise` | bool | no | True | When false, mise.toml is gitignored like mise.local.toml and copied into every new git worktree, and the README leaves out its mise install step. The GitHub workflows install their tools from the committed mise.toml, so they are only offered when it is committed. Any false commit_* answer also gitignores paseo.json and .weft/. |
| `commit_instructions` | bool | no | True | AGENTS.md documents the skills, MCP servers and mise setup, so it defaults to staying out of git whenever one of them does. When false, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are gitignored and copied into every new git worktree. Any false commit_* answer also gitignores paseo.json and .weft/. |
| `package_name` | string | no | example |  |
| `db_type` | string | no | postgres | CUBEJS_DB_TYPE of the warehouse the model reads, as Cube names it (postgres, snowflake, bigquery, databricks-jdbc, redshift, clickhouse, athena, trino, duckdb…: https://docs.cube.dev/admin/connect-to-data). It picks the SQL dialect the check task compiles the golden queries in, and goes into .env.example and, for Kubernetes, each environment's values; the connection itself is set per environment. (e.g. `snowflake`) |
| `use_cube_cloud` | bool | no | False | True for the managed Cube Cloud: pins the cube CLI in mise.toml and adds a deploy task, which uploads cube/ to a deployment, waits for the build and validates the model there. False for self-hosted Cube Core: adds a Dockerfile that bakes the model into Cube's image, and offers a Helm chart for Kubernetes. |
| `cube_deployment_id` | string | no |  | Id of the Cube Cloud deployment the data model deploys to, from its URL or `cube deployments list`. Becomes CUBE_DEPLOYMENT_ID in mise.toml; leave it empty until the deployment exists. Asked for Cube Cloud. (e.g. `4217`) — only asked when `use_cube_cloud` |
| `deploy_cube_cloud` | bool | no | False | Runs the deploy task as the last step of weft new, and again when weft update changes cube/. Needs cube_deployment_id, a deployment set to deploy from the CLI, and `cube login` done (or CUBE_API_URL and CUBE_API_KEY exported) beforehand. Asked for Cube Cloud. — only asked when `use_cube_cloud` |
| `use_helm` | bool | no | False | Adds charts/cube, a production Helm chart for the API instances, the refresh worker and a Cube Store cluster, with its unit tests and an install test on kind, plus deploy/<environment>.yaml values and a deploy task, which ships the data model as an image tagged by its content. Asked for Cube Core. — only asked when `not use_cube_cloud` |
| `deploy_kubernetes` | bool | no | False | Runs `mise run deploy dev` as the last steps of weft new, first for the chart, then for the data model, and again when weft update changes them. Needs a kubectl context, ideally a local cluster such as kind, and the data source connection as exported CUBEJS_* variables, since .env does not exist yet. Asked with the Helm chart. — only asked when `use_helm` |
| `use_github_actions` | bool | no | True | Adds a workflow that runs the check task on every pull request and push to main, and the deploy workflow of the edition: Cube Cloud from main, or Kubernetes from main to staging, then to production once its reviewers approve; with the Helm chart, also the chart's lint, unit tests and kind install. Defaults to whether the project is on GitHub. Only offered when mise.toml is committed, which the workflows install their tools from. — only asked when `commit_mise` |

Secrets are never passed as answers — they resolve from their source
(`env:`/`cmd:`/`prompt`) at render time.

## Presets

Preset answers are locks: the question is skipped interactively and
an explicit `--answer` for it errors. Constraints pin multichoice
options (fixed = always selected, blocked = never selectable).

- **with-cube-cloud**: `use_cube_cloud=true` (locked)
- **no-helm**: `use_cube_cloud=false` (locked), `use_helm=false` (locked)

## Patches

- **base** (inherited): Adds the README with a mise setup recipe and the house .gitignore stanzas for OS junk, editors, environment files, mise.local.toml and Claude Code local settings. Expr segments on the commit_* answers end .gitignore with a stanza for the tooling kept out of git, plus paseo.json and .weft/, and leave the mise recipe out when mise.toml is kept out too.
- **editorconfig** (inherited): Adds the house .editorconfig: UTF-8, LF, final newline, four-space indentation with two spaces for YAML, JSON and TOML, and trailing whitespace kept in Markdown.
- **gitattributes** (inherited): Adds a .gitattributes that stores and checks out every text file with LF line endings.
- **instructions** (inherited): Adds AGENTS.md as the single instruction file, read by Codex and oh-my-pi directly and by Claude Code through a CLAUDE.md that imports it. It records only what is true for every scaffold: mise setup, where skills live, and how MCP servers are declared.
- **mcp** (inherited): Holds the lines .mcp.json (Claude Code), .codex/config.toml (Codex) and .omp/mcp.json (oh-my-pi) share around the slot each MCP server's patch fills, and leaves a file out while no server fills it. Written by weft share from linear-mcp and jira-mcp; change it with weft patch amend.
- **mise** (inherited): Adds mise.toml pinning Node 24 for skill scripts and MCP servers; stack templates add their runtime under [tools], and personal overrides go in the gitignored mise.local.toml.
- **paseo** (inherited): Adds paseo.json, whose setup readies each new Paseo worktree: it runs .agents/seed-worktree.sh from the source checkout, which copies the gitignored local files and whatever the commit_* answers keep out of git, then trusts and installs the mise toolchain. When any of that tooling is kept out of git, paseo.json is gitignored too and Paseo copies it from the source checkout into each new worktree; stack steps appended after it run through mise exec.
- **skills** (inherited): Installs the house Agent Skills that apply to any repository under .agents/skills, the canonical location read by Codex and oh-my-pi; Claude Code reaches them through the symlink farm the sync-claude-skills hook rebuilds.
- **worktree-seed** (inherited): Adds .agents/seed-worktree.sh and links it as git's post-checkout hook, so git worktree add copies the untracked, gitignored local files (.env files, mise.local.toml, Claude Code local settings, and whatever the commit_* answers keep out of git) from the main checkout before any agent starts in the new worktree. It never replaces a file, so paseo.json can run it again as a fallback.
- **anki** (inherited) _(when `use_anki`)_: Installs anki-flashcards and remembering-what-you-built. They talk to AnkiConnect through the anki MCP server, which the anki-mcp patch declares.
- **anki-mcp** (inherited) _(when `use_anki`)_: Declares the anki MCP server whose tools anki-flashcards calls, @ankimcp/anki-mcp-server 0.26.0 run by npx over stdio, for Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi. It talks to AnkiConnect at its default http://localhost:8765, so the entry is the same on every machine and holds no credential.
- **dbt-skills** (inherited) _(when `'dbt' in stack_skills`)_: Installs the house SQL and dbt Agent Skills under .agents/skills: the general SQL rules, writing and documenting models, adding unit tests and the tag conventions, next to the general skills the skills patch provides.
- **github** (inherited) _(when `use_github`)_: Installs the skills for GitHub issues, pull requests, review replies, READMEs, contributor documentation and repository metadata, and one that schedules a pull request for a later day: it moves the branch's commit dates onto that day and leaves a Paseo heartbeat on the agent that was asked, which rebases the branch onto its base and opens the pull request then. They drive gh; GitHub's MCP server is declared by the github-mcp patch.
- **github-mcp** (inherited) _(when `use_github`)_: Declares GitHub's remote MCP server, github at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/, for Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi. The server takes a personal access token from these hosts, so each person exports one as GITHUB_PAT_TOKEN, which the entries name rather than hold.
- **jira** (inherited) _(when `use_jira`)_: Installs the Jira conventions and the skill for writing tickets through an Atlassian MCP server, which the jira-mcp patch declares.
- **jira-mcp** (inherited) _(when `use_jira`)_: Declares Atlassian's remote MCP server for Jira, atlassian at https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp, for Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi. Definition only: each person authorises with OAuth, so nothing is stored in the repository.
- **lightdash-skills** (inherited) _(when `'lightdash' in stack_skills`)_: Installs Lightdash's Agent Skills under .agents/skills, generated by the Lightdash CLI's install-skills at the version its command pins, the one dbt's lightdash patch pins too: developing-in-lightdash for the semantic layer and content as code, effective-dbt-sql, and upgrade-preflight. The installer's version manifests are dropped, so lightdash --version never advises a reinstall over the .claude/skills symlinks; weft update keeps the skills current.
- **linear** (inherited) _(when `use_linear`)_: Installs the Linear conventions and the skills for tracking work, reviewing a team's items and writing project updates. The Linear MCP server itself is declared by the linear-mcp patch.
- **linear-mcp** (inherited) _(when `use_linear`)_: Declares Linear's remote MCP server, linear-server at https://mcp.linear.app/mcp, for Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi. Definition only: each person authorises with OAuth, so nothing is stored in the repository.
- **meetings** (inherited) _(when `use_meetings`)_: Installs preparing-client-meetings, which turns pull requests and tracker tickets into what to say at dailies and weeklies, in a weekly note in the user's Obsidian vault, and writes a pull request scheduled for a later day into the first meeting after it opens. The vault is found on the local filesystem and the trackers are read through the MCP servers the project already has.
- **obsidian** (inherited) _(when `use_obsidian`)_: Installs idea-garden, which files ideas into the user's Obsidian vault through the Obsidian MCP server that the obsidian-mcp patch declares, or directly on the filesystem.
- **obsidian-mcp** (inherited) _(when `use_obsidian`)_: Declares the MCP server that Obsidian's Local REST API with MCP plugin serves, obsidian at http://127.0.0.1:27123/mcp/, for Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi. Each person turns on the plugin's HTTP server and exports its API key as OBSIDIAN_MCP_API_KEY, which the entries name rather than hold.
- **weft** (inherited) _(when `use_weft`)_: Installs weft-conventions, the house conventions for Weft templates, and the skills for creating a template, extracting one from a working project and splitting one in two.
- **writing-slides** (inherited) _(when `'slides' in stack_skills`)_: Installs the writing-slides Agent Skill under .agents/skills: how to turn material into a talk of one-idea slides with sentence headlines, visual evidence, builds, code that fits and steps through, and speaker notes, with this deck's syntax and measured limits, its failure modes, and pnpm check followed by a look at every slide, next to the general skills the skills patch provides.
- **cube**: Adds the Cube project under cube/: an empty cube.py, an example cube on inline rows with the view clients query over it, and .env.example with the data source type. compose.yaml and the dev task run Cube in development mode on this machine, on ports .env can move; every task is a mise file task in .mise/tasks, README.md replaces base's with the setup and the dev loop, and the Cube ignores go at the top of base's .gitignore.
- **model-checks**: Adds the check task, to run before a pull request: it starts compose.yaml's Cube in production mode without a data source connection, compiles the model, and compares the SQL Cube generates for each golden query in tests/queries with the snapshot beside it, writing the snapshots in the project's own dialect on the first run and on --update. README.md and AGENTS.md gain the rule that it passes before every pull request.
- **ci** _(when `use_github_actions`)_: Adds a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the check task on every pull request and push to main, with Node from mise.toml and the runner's Docker, so the golden queries' SQL changes show in the pull request and a failing check can block the merge.
- **cube-cloud** _(when `use_cube_cloud`)_: Pins the cube CLI from the matching Cube release in mise.toml, with the deployment id in its [env], and adds the deploy task: it uploads cube/ to the deploy branch of that deployment, or of the one it is given, waits for the build and validates the model there against the deployment's own variables and Cube version, refusing a deployment that builds from git, whose next sync would overwrite the upload.
- **image** _(when `not use_cube_cloud`)_: Adds a Dockerfile that copies cube/ into Cube's image and runs it as the unprivileged node user, and the image task, which tags the image with the Cube version and a hash of the data model, so an unchanged model is never built, pushed or rolled out again, and pushes it for amd64 and arm64 to GitHub's registry or CUBE_IMAGE. Self-hosted Cube Core only.
- **cd-cube-cloud** _(when `use_github_actions and use_cube_cloud`)_: Adds a deploy workflow that runs the deploy task on every push to main in the GitHub environment production, whose reviewers can gate it, after an optional staging deployment named by the repository variable CUBE_STAGING_DEPLOYMENT_ID. It authenticates with the environments' CUBE_API_URL variable and CUBE_API_KEY secret, one deploy at a time.
- **helm** _(when `use_helm`)_: Adds charts/cube, a production Helm chart adapted from gadsme's cube and cubestore charts: the API instances behind a Service with an optional Ingress, autoscaler and disruption budget, the refresh worker, and a Cube Store router and workers that list each other by stable name, as non-root, read-only pods that drain on shutdown and start only once they reach the data source and Cube Store and have compiled the model, with a NetworkPolicy around Cube Store, S3, GCS or volume storage, statsd-exporter metrics and a ServiceMonitor. values.schema.json rejects unknown keys and chart-owned variables; the chart:lint, chart:test and chart:docs tasks run helm lint with kubeconform, helm-unittest and helm-docs, pinned in mise.toml, and the check task runs the first two.
- **kubernetes** _(when `use_helm`)_: Adds deploy/dev.yaml, staging.yaml and production.yaml, each environment's values, and the deploy task: it ships the image of the data model to the cluster (loaded into a local one, pushed for any other), writes the release's Secret from an env file, upgrades the release with rollback on failure and runs helm test, with --chart-only to keep the image that runs. The chart:e2e task installs every component on a throwaway kind cluster against an in-memory DuckDB. kubectl and kind are pinned in mise.toml.
- **cd-kubernetes** _(when `use_github_actions and use_helm`)_: Adds a deploy workflow that, on every push to main, pushes the commit's data model image to GitHub's registry once, then runs the deploy task for the GitHub environment staging and, after it, production, whose reviewers can gate it, each with its own KUBECONFIG and CUBE_ENV secrets, one deploy at a time.
- **ci-chart** _(when `use_github_actions and use_helm`)_: Adds a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the chart's lint, unit tests and README check on every pull request and push to main, then installs the chart with the commit's data model on a throwaway kind cluster with the chart:e2e task.

## Hooks (side-effects, in run order)

`pre` hooks run before any file is written (a failure aborts); `post`
hooks run after. Effects: **check** = read-only/safe, **setup** =
idempotent local, **deploy** = external/irreversible (confirm first).

| phase | effect | label | patch | command | when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pre | check | Verify mise is installed | `mise` | `command -v mise` | — |
| pre | check | Verify Docker is installed | `cube` | `command -v docker` | — |
| post | setup | Initialise the git repository | `base` | `git init -q -b main` | — |
| post | setup | Install the pinned toolchain | `mise` | `mise trust -q && mise install -y` | — |
| post | setup | Mirror .agents/skills into .claude/skills as symlinks | `skills` | `mkdir -p .claude/skills && for d in .agents/skills/*/; do name=$(basename "$d"); ln -sfn "../../.agents/skills/$name" ".claude/skills/$name"; done && find .claude/skills -maxdepth 1 -type l ! -exec test -e {} \; -delete` | — |
| post | setup | Link the worktree seeding script as git's post-checkout hook | `worktree-seed` | `.agents/seed-worktree.sh link-hook` | — |
| post | setup | Generate the Helm chart's README from values.yaml | `helm` | `mise run chart:docs` | — |
| post | setup | Commit the scaffold | `base` | `git add -A && git commit -q -m 'Scaffold repository'` | — |
| post | deploy | Deploy the data model to Cube Cloud | `cube-cloud` | `mise run deploy` | deploy_cube_cloud |
| post | deploy | Install the Helm chart in the current Kubernetes context | `kubernetes` | `mise run deploy dev --chart-only` | deploy_kubernetes |
| post | deploy | Deploy the data model to the current Kubernetes context | `kubernetes` | `mise run deploy dev` | deploy_kubernetes |

## Scaffold

```sh
weft new . <dest> --answer "project_name=Demo Service" --non-interactive
weft new . <dest> --preset with-cube-cloud --answer "project_name=Demo Service" --non-interactive
weft new . <dest> --preset no-helm --answer "project_name=Demo Service" --non-interactive
```

Agents can pass answers as JSON instead of flags:

```sh
weft new . <dest> --answers-json '{"project_name":"Demo Service"}'
```

## Evolve this template

```sh
cd "$(weft session new <patch> --template . --answer "project_name=Demo Service" --non-interactive)"
… edit the worktree files with concrete values …
weft commit --name <patch> --describe "what it does" --yes
```

Run `weft check --json` after any change; independent patches must
commute and every expression must evaluate.
